meta.note: Every figure here is copied from mybornindiaresearch.com/data/cities.json. Do not invent numbers. Slides render at 1080x1350 (4:5). No em dashes, no en dashes.

slides.headline: The middle of the market is the most expensive floor in it.
slides.lede: In Gurgaon, a 60-110 sqm flat costs more per square foot than one above 110 sqm. Size does not buy a discount here. The mid band does.

slides.headline: Every figure we publish carries its source and its date.
slides.lede: Not because it looks rigorous. Because a property number without a date is a rumour, and most of the numbers you will be quoted this year are rumours.
slides.kicker: Where a figure does not exist yet, we mark it as a gap rather than estimate it.

slides.headline: Carpet, built-up, super built-up. What you are actually paying for.
slides.lede: Three numbers describe the same flat. Only one of them is floor you can stand on.

slides.definition: The usable floor inside your walls. What a carpet would cover. This is the number RERA requires a builder to disclose.
slides.note: The only one that describes your actual home.

slides.definition: Carpet, plus the thickness of your walls, plus balconies. Typically 10 to 15 percent above carpet.
slides.note: Still yours. Just not floor you can use.

slides.definition: Built-up, plus your share of lobbies, lifts, corridors, clubhouse and stairs. Often 25 to 40 percent above carpet.
slides.note: The number most price-per-sqft quotes are based on.

slides.headline: A 30 percent loading turns ₹15,000 per sqft into ₹19,500.
slides.lede: Same flat. Same money. Different denominator. When you compare two projects, check which area each price is quoted on before you compare anything else.
slides.kicker: Ask for the carpet-area price. Always.

slides.unit: per square foot, weighted average across size bands
slides.lede: The middle of the Gurgaon market, as measured by the National Housing Bank's residential index.

slides.headline: Four cities, four different floors.
slides.lede: Every figure below is the weighted median rate per square foot, from the same source, on the same date. Comparable, which is rarer than it sounds.
The most expensive of the four, by a distance.
Less than half of Mumbai, on comparable measurement.
The cheapest we cover, and the least covered by anyone else.

reel.concept: Four cities counting down. '₹1 crore buys you' holds, then each city's square footage counts up from 0 and settles, one per beat, Dehradun largest to Mumbai smallest. Ends on the sourced badge.
reel.source: Derived from NHB RESIDEX, as of 2026-03-31

slides.headline: Circle rate is not market rate. The gap is the story.
slides.lede: One is set by the state. One is what people actually pay. Knowing both tells you things neither tells you alone.

slides.definition: The minimum value a state will register a property at. Also called collector rate or ready reckoner rate. It sets your stamp duty floor.
slides.note: Set by government. Revised occasionally, often lagging.

slides.definition: What a buyer and seller actually agree. Can sit well above the circle rate, and in a weak market can sit close to it.

slides.headline: A narrow gap is a cold market. A wide one is a hot market, or a stale circle rate.
slides.lede: You cannot read it in isolation, which is exactly why a single number from a listing site tells you almost nothing about where a market actually is.

slides.headline: Gurgaon rose 22.8 percent in a year. Your flat did not necessarily.
slides.lede: A city index is a basket. It moves with the mix of what transacted, the size bands that sold, and the areas that were active. Your address is not the basket.
slides.kicker: An index tells you about a market. Only a valuation tells you about a property.
slides.source: NHB RESIDEX press release · as of 2025-12-31

slides.headline: Three numbers that should decide where you buy.
slides.lede: Not the brochure render. Not the sample flat. These three, in this order.

slides.definition: Not super built-up. Insist on the carpet number, then compare across projects on that basis alone.
slides.note: Everything else is a different denominator.

slides.definition: How far above the state's own floor is this price. A number far above a recently revised circle rate deserves a question.
From the RERA filing. Is the money coming in faster than the building is going up.
slides.note: The one a broker will not volunteer.

slides.eyebrow: Why we do not quote listings
slides.headline: A listing price is what someone hopes to get.
slides.lede: A registered price is what someone actually got. We build on the second, and it costs us a great deal of convenience to do so.

slides.definition: Abundant, current, free, and available by the million. Also asking prices, posted by the seller's side, with no obligation to reflect any completed transaction.
Registration departments, RERA filings, the National Housing Bank index. Slower, patchier, sometimes behind a captcha or a scanned PDF.
slides.note: But checkable by you, not just by us.

slides.headline: We would rather publish four cities we can defend than forty we cannot.
slides.lede: That is why our coverage looks small. It is also why every figure on it carries a date and a source you can go and read for yourself.
